newsitem.title: DUBAI: Prominent Bonn politician meets officials in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Bonn politician meets officials in Iran.

text.p: An Iranian newspaper said on Monday that visiting German politician Juergen Moellemann had called for the restoration of bilateral diplomatic and economic ties, severed after a Berlin court ruled that Tehran had ordered political killings.

Moellemann, a parliamentarian of the liberal Free Democrats and former economics minister, spoke after meeting Iranian Minister of Mines and Metals Mohammad Hossein Mahlouji in Tehran on Sunday, the daily Tehran Times said.

"I emphasise the need for restoring diplomatic and economic relations between Iran and Germany," Moellemann was quoted as saying. The English-language daily said the officials had discussed cooperation in the field of mines and metals.
The German Embassy in Tehran confirmed Moellemann had been in Tehran for talks, but had returned to Bonn.
"He was here and held technical discussions, (talks) about projects," a German embassy spokesman told Reuters, but did not give further details on the trip.
The paper quoted Mahlouji as saying Tehran wanted good ties with Germany, but it was up to Bonn to make the first move.
"The politicians in Bonn should take the initiative to restore relations and Tehran is interested in having good relations with Germany and Europe," he was quoted as saying.

European Union states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after the court ruled that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of Kurdish dissidents in Germany. Iran has repeatedly denied this.
While the EU later agreed that the ambassadors could return to Tehran, it has suspended ministerial ties as well as its "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Under the critical dialogue policy, the EU had continued to talk to Iran while trying to get it to move closer to the West.
After the April 10 ruling, Moellemann said Germany should intensify its critical dialogue with Iran rather than give it up.
"A Berlin judge cannot decide how we organise our relations with countries around the world," he had said. "If there are problems, one should actually intensify the dialogue."
Bonn's ambassador has still not returned to Tehran.
